title: How many bounces can stand for all eight attempts?
description: A ball is bounced on a bat in eight attempts. The board adds the bounces, divides by the number of attempts, and checks the answer by multiplying it back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the average is the total shared equally over the attempts. Watch for students who divide by the largest count or by the number of different counts instead of the number of attempts.

video_script.why: The child has seen the average as a fair share and now applies it to counts from a ball and bat game.
video_script.substitution: Sharing the total bounces equally over the attempts gives the bounces in one typical attempt.
video_script.anchor: A ball bounced on a bat, with eight attempts of 6, 2, 9, 5, 4, 6, 3 and 5 bounces
video_script.payoff_line: The average is five bounces per attempt

names.{{NAME_4}}: bounces a ball on a bat and counts the bounces before it falls

maths_rules: average = total / number of attempts = 40 / 8 = 5 bounces
video_script.design: The eight counts stay on the board. They are added into a total, shared equally over the eight attempts, and the share is multiplied back to the total.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a ball bounces on a bat and eight attempt cards show their bounces

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the ball bounces on the bat
marks.m3: the eight attempt cards appear with their counts
marks.m4: a question mark rises over the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>{{NAME_4}} bounces a ball on a bat, but this is not cricket.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The bounces before the ball falls are counted in eight attempts.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>What one number of bounces can stand for all eight attempts?

beats.on_screen: the eight attempt cards stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child who is thinking

beats.on_screen: the eight cards slide into one heap, and the heap is dealt out equally back to the eight attempts

marks.g1: the eight cards slide into one heap
marks.g2: the heap is dealt out equally to the eight attempts

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The average shares the total equally over all the attempts.

marks.given: the eight counts are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the bounces in eight attempts are six, two, nine, five, four, six, three and five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the average number of bounces
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the average number of bounces.

marks.s1: the eight counts are added one after another

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, add all the bounces to get the total.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Six plus two plus nine plus five plus four plus six plus three plus five makes forty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, average = total ÷ number of attempts: 40 ÷ 8 = 5

marks.d1: the rule average = total ÷ number of attempts is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, divide the total by the number of attempts.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Forty divided by eight gives five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, check: 5 × 8 = 40, the same as the total

marks.c1: the 5 is repeated across the 8 attempts
marks.c2: the product 40 is matched with the total

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, check by putting the answer back.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Five multiplied by eight is forty, which is the total.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The average is five bounces per attempt.
